title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: BWP Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, officers, management and team members of the BWP Group, including people working for the BWP Group such as contractors, agents and consultants.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: The Chair; the directors (including the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer); and the Managing Director's and/or Chief Executive Officer's direct reports.

tiers.name: Designated Persons (other than the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer)
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Persons distinguished only for clearance: authorised by the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer.

tiers.name: Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Persons distinguished only for clearance: their own Dealings are authorised by the Chair (or, in the Chair's absence, the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee).

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: Sub-group of Designated Persons distinguished only for clearance: where a proposed Dealing relates to the Chair's own interests, the Authorising Officer is the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Connected Parties
tiers.description: A Designated Person's family members who may influence or be influenced by them in dealings with the BWP Group (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependents), and a company or other entity the Designated Person can control (including family trusts or superannuation funds where they are trustee or beneficiary).

definitions.hedging_definition: any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant Securities

windows.start_anchor: end of year balance date (30 June)
windows.end_anchor: midday Perth time of the next business day after the release of the end of year results
midday Perth time of the next business day after the release of the half year results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, Chair or Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer may determine any other period to be a prohibited trading period (additional prohibited period) and may extend or shorten a Blackout Period at any time; notice is given by the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer or the Company Secretary. A decision to refuse or withdraw clearance is final and binding and must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Derivatives (including exchange traded or OTC options, whatever settlement method) are expressly within the Policy's application. Non-designated BWP Personnel face no clearance requirement, only the insider trading prohibition and the Front Page Test.
rules.evidence: Derivatives of those Securities (including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise)

rules.detail: An OTC put/call is a Derivative and so a Dealing. Designated Persons must obtain prior written authorisation before Dealing, outside Blackout Periods, and confirm they hold no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons, or their Connected Parties, wish to Deal in Securities, they must obtain the prior authorisation of the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer or the Chair

rules.detail: Absolute, Board-unwaivable ban on hedging an element of remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal, which covers unvested remuneration.
rules.evidence: (remuneration related hedging) entering into a hedging or similar arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of a Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal.

rules.detail: The same ban extends to remuneration that has vested but remains subject to a disposal restriction (e.g. a holding lock); Board approval cannot be granted for this prohibited Dealing.
rules.evidence: an element of the Designated Person's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal

rules.detail: The remuneration-related hedging ban is expressed as an additional restriction on Designated Persons only; it is not stated to apply to other BWP Personnel.
Once restrictions on disposal lift, hedging is not banned; 'creating a hedge' is itself named as a Dealing, but non-designated BWP Personnel face no clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Once restrictions on disposal lift, the remuneration hedging ban no longer applies; hedging is a named Dealing requiring prior written authorisation.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named; it would be 'any other transfer or creation of an interest in Securities' or an agreement to do so, and so a Dealing, but non-designated BWP Personnel face no clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: any other transfer or creation of an interest in Securities, whether directly, or by arranging for someone else to undertake the dealing on one's behalf

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named; caught as a Dealing requiring prior written authorisation.
rules.evidence: any other transfer or creation of an interest in Securities, whether directly, or by arranging for someone else to undertake the dealing on one's behalf

rules.detail: Absolute, Board-unwaivable ban on entering instruments or transactions to borrow and sell Securities intending to buy them back later.
rules.evidence: (short selling) entering into instruments or transactions to borrow and sell Securities with the intention of buying Securities back at a later date

rules.detail: The short-selling ban is an additional restriction on Designated Persons only; for other BWP Personnel, selling is a Dealing subject only to the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: selling or otherwise disposing of the Securities, whether on-market or off-market

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy or in the enumerated categories of Dealing.
CFDs are expressly listed as an example of a Derivative and so a Dealing; non-designated BWP Personnel face no clearance requirement.
rules.evidence: Derivatives of those Securities (including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise)

rules.detail: CFDs are expressly named as a Derivative and so a Dealing requiring prior written authorisation, unless the CFD in substance amounts to short selling or remuneration hedging, in which case it is an absolute Prohibited Dealing.
rules.evidence: Derivatives of those Securities (including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise)

rules.detail: Absolute, Board-unwaivable ban on entering into a margin loan in respect of Securities.
rules.evidence: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities

rules.detail: A margin loan is named as a Dealing for all BWP Personnel, but the outright ban in 7.2 is an additional restriction limited to Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Absolute, Board-unwaivable ban on creating a security interest or other financial interest in respect of Securities, not limited to margin loans.
rules.evidence: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities

rules.detail: A security interest is named as a Dealing for all BWP Personnel, but the outright ban in 7.2 is an additional restriction limited to Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: The ban on 'creating a security interest or other financial interest ... in respect of Securities' is not limited to margin loans and is a Board-unwaivable prohibited Dealing, so any secured financing arrangement over the collared shares is prohibited outright for Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities ... Board approval cannot be granted for proposed Dealings that are prohibited Dealings.

rules.detail: A security interest or other financial interest is named as a Dealing for all BWP Personnel, but the outright ban in 7.2 applies only to Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities

rules.detail: Absolute, Board-unwaivable intention-based ban on acquiring or disposing of Securities with intention of reversing the position within less than three months.
rules.evidence: (short term acquisitions) an acquisition of Securities with the intention of disposing of some or all of those Securities within a period of less than three months from the date of acquisition

rules.detail: The short-term dealing ban is an additional restriction on Designated Persons only; the Policy states no short-term trading rule for other BWP Personnel.

clearance.tier: Designated Persons (other than the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer)
clearance.approver: Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately following, and not later than three business days after, the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Authorisation ... is taken to be withdrawn in respect of any off-market Dealing not completed within five business days, or in respect of any on-market Dealing where the relevant trade has not been entered into within ten business days.

clearance.tier: Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer
clearance.approver: Chair of the Board (or, in the Chair's absence, the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately following, and not later than three business days after, the Dealing
clearance.evidence: the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer must advise the Chair of the Board (or in the Chair's absence, the independent chair of the Audit & Risk Committee) in writing ... of their intention to Deal in Securities

clearance.approver: the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee
clearance.post_trade_deadline: immediately following, and not later than three business days after, the Dealing
clearance.evidence: Authorising Officer means the Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer ... (or the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee, where the proposed Dealing relates to the Chair's ... interests

short_term.basis: from the date of acquisition or the date of the sale or disposal
short_term.evidence: an acquisition of Securities with the intention of disposing of some or all of those Securities within a period of less than three months from the date of acquisition ... disposing of Securities with the intention of buying Securities back within a period of less than three months from the sale or disposal

exceptions.evidence: transfers of Securities between a Designated Person and Connected Parties, or by a Designated Person to their superannuation fund, in respect of which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with this Policy
a disposal of Securities arising from the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back
a disposal of rights acquired, or acquisition of, Securities under a pro-rata issue

an acquisition of Securities under a security purchase plan or distribution reinvestment plan where the BWP Personnel did not commence or amend their participation in the plan during a Blackout Period

an acquisition or disposal of Securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan where ... the plan does not permit the BWP Personnel to exercise any discretion over how, when, or whether to acquire or dispose of Securities
an acquisition of Securities under the BWP Group's employee incentive scheme, or the conversion of a convertible Security
Dealings by BWP Personnel as a trustee, provided they are not a beneficiary of the trust and the decision to trade is taken by other directors or trustees of the trust independent of them

where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or conversion of the Security falls during a Blackout Period and the BWP Personnel could not reasonably be expected to have exercised the option or right during a permitted trading period

indirect and incidental trading that occurs as a consequence of a BWP Personnel Dealing in Securities issued by a managed investment scheme, listed investment company, exchange traded fund or similar investment vehicle that is managed by a third party
severe financial hardship or has a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling their relevant Securities of the BWP Group Member

required by a court order, or there are court enforceable undertakings, to transfer or sell Securities of the BWP Group Member, or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement for them to do so

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer (Managing Director and/or Chief Executive Officer, or the Chair/independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee as applicable) may waive the Blackout Period restriction, but not any Prohibited Dealing under 7.2, in exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order; clearance can be given or refused without reasons, is final and binding, may be withdrawn on new information, and the Authorising Officer may refer the matter to the Board for approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (security or margin interests) creating a security interest or other financial interest, or entering into a margin loan, in respect of Securities ... Board approval cannot be granted for proposed Dealings that are prohibited Dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar -- any security interest over the shares, not just a margin loan -- is an absolute, Board-unwaivable prohibition for Designated Persons (the Chair, all directors including the MD/CEO, and their direct reports), so the structure cannot be cleared under any circumstances for this tier.

bespoke_clauses.topic: remuneration hedging ban tied to disposal restriction, not vesting
bespoke_clauses.clause: entering into a hedging or similar arrangement (with anyone) if the arrangement would have the effect of limiting the exposure of a Designated Person to risk relating to an element of the Designated Person's remuneration that remains subject to restrictions on disposal.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This ban follows the disposal restriction rather than the vesting date -- shares that have vested but remain subject to a holding lock cannot be collared -- and it is also an unwaivable prohibited Dealing.

bespoke_clauses.topic: hedge and security interest expressly named as Dealings
bespoke_clauses.clause: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to the Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs of a collar (the hedge/derivative and the secured loan) are expressly named as Dealings, removing any argument that a bespoke OTC structure falls outside the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: [The excluded dealings in section 9 do not include a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights.]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Designated Persons cannot create a security interest at all, the Policy provides no carve-out for a lender's enforcement sale; secured financing is simply unavailable for this tier rather than merely restricted.

bespoke_clauses.topic: off-market authorisation lapses in 5 business days
bespoke_clauses.clause: is taken to be withdrawn in respect of any off-market Dealing not completed within five business days, or in respect of any on-market Dealing where the relevant trade has not been entered into within ten business days.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An OTC collar is an off-market Dealing, so any authorisation to enter it (for the non-prohibited, vested-unrestricted hedge leg) lapses after 5 business days and must be re-sought if not executed in time.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Dealings that would not satisfy The Front Page Test should not occur, even where the Dealing may not strictly be prohibited under the Policy or otherwise at law.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the permitted hedge-only leg for a Designated Person could be discouraged or refused on reputational grounds beyond the strict legal analysis.

summary: A funded collar is not available to Designated Persons (the Chair, all directors including the Managing Director/CEO, and the MD/CEO's direct reports) under this Policy: creating any security interest or other financial interest, or entering a margin loan, over BWP securities is an express, unwaivable 'Prohibited Dealing' for which 'Board approval cannot be granted', and hedging any element of remuneration still subject to disposal restrictions is separately and equally unwaivable. Once shares vest and any disposal restriction lifts, hedging is not itself banned and, together with an OTC put/call and any monetisation, is an ordinary Dealing (hedges and derivatives are expressly named) requiring prior written authorisation from the Managing Director/CEO (or the Chair for the MD/CEO's own dealing, or the independent chair of the Audit and Risk Committee for the Chair's own dealing), confined outside Blackout Periods and lapsing after 5 business days for an off-market transaction. For BWP Personnel who are not Designated Persons, none of the 7.2 prohibitions apply -- margin loans, security interests and hedges are all merely Dealings subject only to the insider trading rules and the Front Page Test, so a funded collar would in principle be workable for that group, though they are unlikely to be the bank's target clients. Because the security-interest ban is absolute for Designated Persons, the Policy provides no secured-lender enforcement carve-out and no financing disclosure regime for that tier. Overall, the funded collar as a whole is blocked for the directors and executives the bank is targeting, and only an unfunded, hedge-only structure could be contemplated for them, subject to authorisation.
